newsitem.title: USA: Aetrium year-end order backlog $17 mln.
newsitem.headline: Aetrium year-end order backlog $17 mln.

text.p: Aetrium Inc said its backlog of unfilled orders exceeded $17 million at year-end.

"We are cautiously optimistic as we start 1997," said chief executive Joseph Levesque. "We expect a gradual improvement in industry conditions. Regardless of improved conditions, we will continue to operate conservatively, and we plan to add to our backlog during the first half of the year."
Aetrium reported Thursday that net income for 1996 was $9.2 million, up 19 percent from 1995, excluding an acquisition-related charge in 1995.
Annual revenues were $58.3 million, up 23 percent compared with 1995. The company makes test-handling solutions for the semiconductor industry.
Bookings at the start of the fourth quarter were slow, but increased appreciably in November and December, Aetrium said.

"For the quarter, our book-to-bill ratio was near parity, as we have continued to see signs that indicate we have turned the corner," the company said. "Newer product offerings sold well throughout 1996, and in the fourth quarter we began to see an increase in orders for our more mature products, as customers once again added to their production capacity."

Consolidated gross margin fell in 1996 to 55.1 percent from 57.1 percent in 1995. "The decline was largely due to the December 1995 acquisition of E.J. Systems, a maker of thermal conditioning equipment," Aetrium said.
"Gross margin at E.J. Systems increased throughout 1996, but we still have some work to do in 1997 to get gross margin to our planned level."
